# mime - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/mime/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#mime)Mime

Mime is now Media Type, technically, but `Mime` is more immediately
understandable, so the main type here is `Mime`.

[§](https://docs.rs#what-is-mime)What is Mime?

Example mime string: `text/plain`

```
let plain_text: mime::Mime = "text/plain".parse().unwrap();
assert_eq!(plain_text, mime::TEXT_PLAIN);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#inspecting-mimes)Inspecting Mimes

```
let mime = mime::TEXT_PLAIN;
match (mime.type_(), mime.subtype()) {
    (mime::TEXT, mime::PLAIN) => println!("plain text!"),
    (mime::TEXT, _) => println!("structured text"),
    _ => println!("not text"),
}
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [From](https://docs.rs/struct.FromStrError.html)- StrError
- An error when parsing a `Mime`from a string.
- [Mime](https://docs.rs/struct.Mime.html)
- A parsed mime or media type.
- [Mime](https://docs.rs/struct.MimeIter.html)- Iter
- An iterator of parsed mime
- [Name](https://docs.rs/struct.Name.html)
- A section of a `Mime`.
- [Params](https://docs.rs/struct.Params.html)
- An iterator over the parameters of a MIME.

# mime 0.3.17 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/mime/latest

# mime

Support MIME (Media Types) as strong types in Rust.

## Usage

```
extern crate mime;
// common types are constants
let text = TEXT_PLAIN;
// deconstruct Mimes to match on them
match
```
Support MIME (Media Types) as strong types in Rust.

```
extern crate mime;
// common types are constants
let text = mime::TEXT_PLAIN;
// deconstruct Mimes to match on them
match (text.type_(), text.subtype()) {
    (mime::TEXT, mime::PLAIN) => {
        // plain text!
    },
    (mime::TEXT, _) => {
        // structured text!
    },
    _ => {
        // not text!
    }
}
```

# About Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/about

Docs.rs is an
            [open source](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs)
            documentation host for crates of the
            [Rust Programming Language](https://www.rust-lang.org/).
            All libraries published to [crates.io](https://crates.io)
            are documented. If you just published a crate, your crate is likely
            still in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

            The source code of Docs.rs is available on
            [GitHub](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs). If
            you ever encounter an issue, don't hesitate to report it! (And
            thanks in advance!)

Currently running Docs.rs version is: **0.0.0 (964c90a45859fd8f9076e3cbe58470a5a4f4d4f7 2026-07-01 )**

Summaries of the documentation build processes [are available at /releases/](https://docs.rs/releases).

            JavaScript in support of documentation is allowed but not guaranteed to work on docs.rs. What that
            means: If you write documentation that inlines some JavaScript (like
            [KaTeX](https://katex.org/)), that's allowed, and
            will probably work today but may break in the future.

However, it's not allowed to put JavaScript or other content in docs published on docs.rs for the purpose of tracking visitors. For instance, adding Google Analytics scripts, tracking pixels, or site verification for services like Google Search Console. Crates that do this will have the relevant versions removed and may be blocked from docs.rs.

            Docs.rs is run and maintained by the [Docs.rs team](https://www.rust-lang.org/governance/teams/dev-tools#team-docs-rs).
            You can find us in #t-docs-rs on [Zulip](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/356853-t-docs-rs).

---

# Badges

Source: https://docs.rs/about/badges

Docs.rs no longer has its own badges. Consider using [shields.io](https://shields.io) instead.

# Builds

Source: https://docs.rs/about/builds

Docs.rs automatically builds documentation for crates released on [crates.io](https://crates.io/).
                It may take a while to build your crate, depending on how many crates are in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

                All crates are built in a sandbox using the nightly release of the Rust compiler.
                The current version in use is `rustc 1.98.0-nightly (4c9d2bfe4 2026-07-01)`.

                The README displayed on docs.rs follows Cargo’s `package.readme` rules.
                If `readme` is not set, docs.rs will look for `README.md`, `README.txt`, or `README` in the crate root.
                Set `readme = "path/to/file"` to use a custom file, `readme = true` to use `README.md`, or `readme = false` to disable the README.

                To recognize Docs.rs from your Rust code, you can test for the `docsrs` cfg, e.g.:

```
```
                To recognize Docs.rs from `build.rs` files, you can test for the environment variable `DOCS_RS`, e.g.:

`if var.is_ok `
              All targets other than `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` are cross-compiled. For implementation reasons, this is unlikely to change for the foreseeable future.

                You can configure how your crate is built by adding [package metadata](https://docs.rs/metadata) to your `Cargo.toml`, e.g.:

```
[]
 = ["--cfg", "my_cfg"]
```
`#[cfg(my_cfg)]` (not to be confused with `#[cfg(doc)]`) can be used for conditional compilation.
                This approach is also useful for setting
                When you start using docs.rs metadata or `#[cfg(docsrs)]` in your code, you might run into issues
                where your code builds fine locally but fails on docs.rs.
                To avoid this, you can add [ cargo docs-rs](https://github.com/dtolnay/cargo-docs-rs) to
                your test-suite.
                While it doesn't perfectly replicate our build environment, it can catch many common issues.

                The Docs.rs [README](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/blob/master/README.md#build-subcommand) describes how to build
                unpublished crate documentation locally using the same build environment as the Docs.rs build agent.

                Missing dependencies are a common reason for failed builds.
                Docs.rs dependencies are managed through
                [crates-build-env](https://github.com/rust-lang/crates-build-env).
                See [Forge](https://forge.rust-lang.org/docs-rs/add-dependencies.html) for how to add a dependency.

                Most of the sandbox is a read-only file system, including the source directory of your crate and its dependencies.
                If your `build.rs` generates files that are relevant for documentation, consider writing to the
                [cargo output directory](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/environment-variables.html#environment-variables-cargo-sets-for-crates),
                passed in the environment variable `OUT_DIR`.

All the builds are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The current limits are:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                If your build fails because it hit one of these limits, please
                [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                to get them increased for your crate.
                Since our build agent has finite resources, we have to consider each case individually. However, there are a few general policies:

If your crate fails to build for a reason not listed here, you can rebuild it from [crates.io](https://crates.io) website as you can see below:

Or you can [file an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues) if you think it's a **docs.rs** issue.

# Metadata

Source: https://docs.rs/about/metadata

You can customize docs.rs builds by defining `[package.metadata.docs.rs]`
		table in your crates' `Cargo.toml`.

The available configuration flags you can customize are:

```
[]
 = "test"
[]
# Features to pass to Cargo (default: [])
 = ["feature1", "feature2"]
# Whether to pass `--all-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Whether to pass `--no-default-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Target to test build on, used as the default landing page (default: "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu")
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
 = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
# Targets to build (default: see below)
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
#
# Default targets:
# - x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - aarch64-apple-darwin
# - x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
# - aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - i686-pc-windows-msvc
#
# Set this to `[]` to only build the default target.
#
# If `default-target` is unset, the first element of `targets` is treated as the default target.
# Otherwise, these `targets` are built in addition to the default target.
# If both `default-target` and `targets` are unset,
#   all tier-one targets will be built and `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` will be used as the default target.
 = ["aarch64-apple-darwin", "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"]
# If you want to instead add another target without overwriting the default ones:
 = ["i686-apple-darwin"]
# Additional `RUSTFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustc-arg"]
# Additional `RUSTDOCFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustdoc-arg"]
# List of command line arguments for `cargo`.
#
# These cannot be a subcommand, they may only be options.
 = ["-Z", "build-std"]
```

# Shorthand URLs

Source: https://docs.rs/about/redirections

Docs.rs uses semver to parse URLs. You can use this feature to access
            crates' documentation easily. Example of URL redirections for
            `clap` crate:

| URL | Redirects to documentation of |
|---|---|
| [docs.rs/clap](https://docs.rs/clap) | Latest version of clap |
| [docs.rs/clap::Command](https://docs.rs/clap::Command) | Latest version of clap, and search for "Command" within the crate |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2) | 2.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2.9](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2.9) | 2.9.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/2.9.3](https://docs.rs/clap/2.9.3) | 2.9.3 version (you don't need `=`unlike semver) |
| [docs.rs/clap/*](https://docs.rs/clap/*) | Latest version of this page (if it still exists). "latest" or "newest" work as well as `*`. |

---

# Download

Source: https://docs.rs/about/download

docs.rs stores the `rustdoc` output in a ZIP file.

                These archives can be used as a base for further processing of
                the documentation for offline readers like Dash or Zeal.
                **They are not directly usable for offline documentation.**

The download is possible for specific or semantic versions:

But also viaTo unpack the ZIP file you need any zip utility that supports PKZIP version 4.6 and BZIP2 & Deflate compression.

The archives will contain all the documentation HTML files for all targets and CSS/JS assets that are specific to the build. The default target will be found at the root, and other targets each in its own subfolder.

                Docs.rs is running rustdoc with `--static-root-path "/-/rustdoc.static/"`,
                which leads to all references to static assets breaking if they are not
                available under that path. Older builds used `--static-root-path "/"`, which
                means you will have to handle both.

                Since we're also adding `--emit=invocation-specific` to our build
                the archives will *not* contain any static assets that are specific to the
                toolchain. For now these will have to be downloaded file-by-file directly
                from docs.rs.

---

# Rustdoc JSON

Source: https://docs.rs/about/rustdoc-json

docs.rs builds & hosts the [ rustdoc JSON](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustdoc/unstable-features.html#json-output) output.

This structured version of the documentation can be used for inspecting the docs and types of the crate in a programmatic way.

                The JSON file you're downloading might have been built with an older version of `rustdoc`
                so you might have to check the `format_version` attribute to determine how to parse the structure.
                The [ rustdoc-types](https://docs.rs/rustdoc-types/) crate helps with this.

**
                We started building rustdoc JSON on 2025-05-23. So any release before that won't have a download
                available until our rebuilds reached that release.
            **

                The download URLs can be generic or specific, depending on what you need. In case of rebuilds we
                also keep old format versions around. **Until we rebuilt all releases, we might return
                a `404 NOT FOUND` for some.**

By default we use `zstd` compression, which is more space efficient and faster to decompress. For more limited environments we also started supporting `gzip` compression. You can receive gzip by adding `.gz` to the given URL.

Here some URL examples you can use.

| URL | Redirects to JSON download of |
|---|---|
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json) | latest version, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz) | latest version, default target, latest format-version, gzip compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42) | latest version, default target, format-version 42 |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json.zst](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json.zst) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version, zstd compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json) | latest version, windows target, latest format-version |

# polkadot_node_primitives - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/polkadot-node-primitives/26.0.0/polkadot_node_primitives/

## Expand description

Primitive types used on the node-side.

Unlike the `polkadot-primitives` crate, these primitives are only used on the node-side,
not shared between the node and the runtime. This crate builds on top of the primitives defined
there.

# anoma_generic_call_library - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/anoma-generic-call-library/1.0.0/anoma_generic_call_library/

## Expand description

Host-side prover for GenericCall resource logic.

`GENERIC_CALL_ELF` and `GENERIC_CALL_ID` are placeholders. After building
the guest with the RISC0 toolchain (`cd crates/generic_call_circuit && cargo build`),
copy the output ELF to `elf/generic-call-guest.bin` and update `GENERIC_CALL_ID`
with the printed image ID.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [GENERIC_](https://docs.rs/struct.GENERIC_CALL_ID.html)- CALL_ - ID
- [Generic](https://docs.rs/struct.GenericCall.html)- Call
- A single EVM call to forward.
- [Generic](https://docs.rs/struct.GenericCallLogic.html)- Call - Logic
- Wraps a `GenericCallWitness`and implements`LogicProver`so it can be used for proof generation inside the RISC0 zkVM.

# scryone - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/scryone/0.2.0/scryone/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#scryone)Scryone

Crate for providing an API Client, Types, and Request objects for working with the [Scryfall
API](https://scryfall.com/docs/api)

It offers the following:

- Types to represent Scryfall Objects (e.g. Cards, Sets, Rulings etc).
- Asynchronous and blocking API Clients to communicate with Scryfall
- Request types and builders for building requests to each of Scryfall API’s endpoints

[§](https://docs.rs#requests)Requests

Scryfall has many endpoints for different aspects of their API.
To help you execute queries against certain endpoints, `scryone` provides
[ Request](https://docs.rs/api/request/index.html) types and
builders for them which allow you to set all parameters that Scryfall allows.

Each Request type implements a trait called [ ScryfallRequest](https://docs.rs/api/request/trait.ScryfallRequest.html) which automatically builds the appropriate URL
for the API based on the parameters that you have set.

For example, creating a request to search for a specific card (`/cards/search` endpoint in
Scryfall):

```
let request = CardSearchRequest::builder()
    .query("Winter Orb")
    .unique_mode(UniqueMode::Cards)
    .sort_order(SortOrder::Set)
    .sort_direction(SortDirection::Desc)
    .data_format(DataFormat::Json)
    .build()?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#api-clients)API Clients

An [ asynchronous](https://docs.rs/api/struct.ScryfallClient.html) and

[client are supplied to enable you to contact Scryfall’s API.](https://docs.rs/api/blocking/struct.ScryfallClient.html)

`blocking`The clients offer the following:

-
GET requests to the endpoint that accepts a `ScryfallRequest`
-
POST requests to endpoints that allow it (only one single API endpoints supports this as of now).
-
Generic GET requests that allow you to define the type you wish to deserialize into (you must provide the URL)
-
Paginated requests that automatically (and respectfully) retrieve all data from paginated responses from Scryfall.

Example:

```
let client = ScryfallClient::new();
let request = CardSearchRequest::builder()
    .query("Winter Orb")
    .unique_mode(UniqueMode::Cards)
    .sort_order(SortOrder::Set)
    .sort_direction(SortDirection::Desc)
    .data_format(DataFormat::Json)
    .build()?;
// Automatically constructs the appropriate URL for the `/cards/search` endpoint
let response: List<Vec<Card>> = client.get(request).await?;
println!("Total cards: {:?}", response.total_cards);
println!("Cards: {:?}", response.data);
```

# sim_lib_discrete_comb - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-discrete-comb/0.1.0-rc.1/sim_lib_discrete_comb/

## Expand description

Discrete combinatorics.

This crate hosts exact counting functions (over `num_bigint::BigUint`), lazy
enumerators, and canonical combinadic / Lehmer / mixed-radix rank-unrank
helpers. These ordinals are the bridge to rank, but this crate never depends
on `sim-lib-rank`.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [bit_](https://docs.rs/bit_vector/index.html)- vector
- Fixed-width bit vectors in natural binary order, with rank/unrank.
- [cards](https://docs.rs/cards/index.html)
- Browse/help card content for the combinatorics family, as static data.
- [combination](https://docs.rs/combination/index.html)
- `k`-combinations of- `{0, ..., n-1}`in lexicographic order, with rank/unrank.
- [count](https://docs.rs/count/index.html)
- Exact combinatorial counting functions over `num_bigint::BigUint`.
- [error](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)
- Error type for discrete combinatorics.
- [mixed_](https://docs.rs/mixed_radix/index.html)- radix
- Bounded integer vectors under a mixed-radix numeral system, with rank/unrank.
- [partition](https://docs.rs/partition/index.html)
- Integer partitions of `n`in ascending-composition order (Kelleher’s`accel_asc`). The iterator is genuinely lazy, so large`n`is safe to start.
- [permutation](https://docs.rs/permutation/index.html)
- Permutations of `{0, ..., n-1}`in lexicographic order, with Lehmer-code rank/unrank.
- [subset](https://docs.rs/subset/index.html)
- Subsets of `{0, ..., n-1}`in bitmask order, with rank/unrank.

# viterbi - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/viterbi/0.0.1/viterbi/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#viterbi--ccsds-k7-r12-convolutional-encoder--hard-decision-block-viterbi-decoder)`viterbi` — CCSDS K=7 R=1/2 convolutional encoder + hard-decision block Viterbi decoder.

This crate is the **inner code** of the classic CCSDS concatenated coding scheme
(`K = 7`, `R = 1/2`), designed to pair with an outer Reed–Solomon code via an interleaver:

```
TX:  data → [RS(255,223)] → [interleaver] → [conv. K=7] → CHANNEL
RX:  CHANNEL → [Viterbi] → [de-interleaver] → [RS decode] → data
               └── this crate
```
This increment (`v0.0.x`) provides **hard-decision, block-mode** encode/decode targeting `std`.
Soft-decision, puncturing, rate 1/3, and generic `K ≤ 9` are additive in the next minor.

[§](https://docs.rs#design-invariants)Design invariants

- Pure Rust, no `unsafe`(`forbid`ed crate-wide via`Cargo.toml`lints and here).
- Deterministic: same input ⇒ same output, bit-for-bit, on every platform.
- No panic in the decode hot path; `Result`only at configuration boundaries.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Encode a payload, then recover it with the Viterbi decoder (clean channel):

```
use viterbi::{CcsdsViterbiDecoder, CodeParams, ViterbiEncoder};
// Build the encoder and decoder from the first-class CCSDS profile.
let encoder = ViterbiEncoder::new(CodeParams::ccsds_r1_2()).unwrap();
let mut decoder = CcsdsViterbiDecoder::new(CodeParams::ccsds_r1_2(), 4096).unwrap();
let payload = b"hello, viterbi";
let coded = encoder.encode(payload).unwrap();
let decoded = decoder.decode_block(&coded).unwrap();
assert_eq!(&decoded.bytes, payload);
```
## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use decoder::`- [CcsdsViterbiDecoder](https://docs.rs/decoder/type.CcsdsViterbiDecoder.html);
- `pub use decoder::`- [ConfigError](https://docs.rs/decoder/enum.ConfigError.html);
- `pub use decoder::`- [DecodeError](https://docs.rs/decoder/enum.DecodeError.html);
- `pub use decoder::`- [ViterbiDecoder](https://docs.rs/decoder/struct.ViterbiDecoder.html);
- `pub use encoder::`- [EncodeError](https://docs.rs/encoder/enum.EncodeError.html);
- `pub use encoder::`- [ViterbiEncoder](https://docs.rs/encoder/struct.ViterbiEncoder.html);
- `pub use metric::`- [BranchMetric](https://docs.rs/metric/trait.BranchMetric.html);
- `pub use metric::`- [HardHamming](https://docs.rs/metric/struct.HardHamming.html);
- `pub use metric::`- [HARD_ERASURE](https://docs.rs/metric/constant.HARD_ERASURE.html);
- `pub use packing::`- [CodedBlock](https://docs.rs/packing/struct.CodedBlock.html);
- `pub use packing::`- [DecodedBlock](https://docs.rs/packing/struct.DecodedBlock.html);
- `pub use params::`- [CodeParams](https://docs.rs/params/struct.CodeParams.html);
- `pub use params::`- [ParamError](https://docs.rs/params/enum.ParamError.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [decoder](https://docs.rs/decoder/index.html)
- Hard-decision block Viterbi decoder (ACS + traceback).
- [encoder](https://docs.rs/encoder/index.html)
- Convolutional encoder with zero-tail termination (R1, R2).
- [metric](https://docs.rs/metric/index.html)
- Branch-metric abstraction: hard-decision Hamming now, soft/erasure-ready (R7).
- [packing](https://docs.rs/packing/index.html)
- MSB-first bit <-> byte packing and the block wrappers (R16). Sole owner of this conversion.
- [params](https://docs.rs/params/index.html)
- Convolutional code parameters and their validation (R8, R19).

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [K](https://docs.rs/constant.K.html)
- Constraint length.
- [M](https://docs.rs/constant.M.html)
- Memory (shift-register length) = K - 1.
- [MAX_](https://docs.rs/constant.MAX_SUPPORTED_INFO_BITS.html)- SUPPORTED_ - INFO_ - BITS
- Hard upper bound on `max_info_bits`(R18).
- [N](https://docs.rs/constant.N.html)
- Output bits per input bit (rate 1/2).
- [STATES](https://docs.rs/constant.STATES.html)
- Trellis states for the CCSDS profile = 2^M.

# knok - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/knok/0.3.2/knok/

## Expand description

Static-shape tensor containers and runtime wrappers for build-time traced IREE VM bytecode artifacts.

Graphs are authored from `build.rs` with `knok-build`, which executes traced
Rust functions on the compile host and writes generated artifact wrappers to
`OUT_DIR`. Target crates import those wrappers with `generated_graphs!`:

For repeated hosted inference, construct one [ Engine](https://docs.rs/runtime/struct.Engine.html) and call generated

`graphs::<name>::run(&engine, ...)` wrappers.With default features disabled, `knok` is `no_std + alloc`; hosted runtime
execution is unavailable on the target unless the runtime feature set is
enabled.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use artifact::`- [DType](https://docs.rs/artifact/enum.DType.html);
- `pub use artifact::`- [GraphArtifact](https://docs.rs/artifact/struct.GraphArtifact.html);
- `pub use artifact::`- [GraphArtifactVariant](https://docs.rs/artifact/struct.GraphArtifactVariant.html);
- `pub use artifact::`- [TensorDesc](https://docs.rs/artifact/struct.TensorDesc.html);
- `pub use backend::`- [Backend](https://docs.rs/backend/enum.Backend.html);
- `pub use backend::`- [Driver](https://docs.rs/backend/enum.Driver.html);
- `pub use backend::`- [SUPPORTED_BACKENDS](https://docs.rs/backend/constant.SUPPORTED_BACKENDS.html);
- `pub use graph::`- [Graph](https://docs.rs/graph/struct.Graph.html);
- `pub use runtime::`- [Engine](https://docs.rs/runtime/struct.Engine.html);
- `pub use runtime::`- [RuntimeConfig](https://docs.rs/runtime/struct.RuntimeConfig.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [artifact](https://docs.rs/artifact/index.html)
- Static metadata for generated graph artifacts.
- [backend](https://docs.rs/backend/index.html)
- Backend and runtime driver identifiers supported by generated artifacts. Supported IREE compiler backends and runtime drivers.
- [graph](https://docs.rs/graph/index.html)
- Typed generated graph handles and runtime boundary traits.
- [prelude](https://docs.rs/prelude/index.html)
- Common imports for target crates that call generated graph wrappers.
- [runtime](https://docs.rs/runtime/index.html)
- [tensor](https://docs.rs/tensor/index.html)
- Fixed-rank tensor containers used by generated graph wrappers.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [generated_](https://docs.rs/macro.generated_graphs.html)- graphs
- Includes graph wrapper modules generated by `knok-build`into the target crate.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html)
- Errors returned by tensor construction and hosted runtime execution.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Result](https://docs.rs/type.Result.html)
- Result alias used by the public runtime and tensor APIs.

# mime 0.3.17 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/mime/0.3.17

# mime

Support MIME (Media Types) as strong types in Rust.

## Usage

```
extern crate mime;
// common types are constants
let text = TEXT_PLAIN;
// deconstruct Mimes to match on them
match
```
Support MIME (Media Types) as strong types in Rust.

```
extern crate mime;
// common types are constants
let text = mime::TEXT_PLAIN;
// deconstruct Mimes to match on them
match (text.type_(), text.subtype()) {
    (mime::TEXT, mime::PLAIN) => {
        // plain text!
    },
    (mime::TEXT, _) => {
        // structured text!
    },
    _ => {
        // not text!
    }
}
```

# mime - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/mime/0.3.17/target-redirect/mime/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#mime)Mime

Mime is now Media Type, technically, but `Mime` is more immediately
understandable, so the main type here is `Mime`.

[§](https://docs.rs#what-is-mime)What is Mime?

Example mime string: `text/plain`

```
let plain_text: mime::Mime = "text/plain".parse().unwrap();
assert_eq!(plain_text, mime::TEXT_PLAIN);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#inspecting-mimes)Inspecting Mimes

```
let mime = mime::TEXT_PLAIN;
match (mime.type_(), mime.subtype()) {
    (mime::TEXT, mime::PLAIN) => println!("plain text!"),
    (mime::TEXT, _) => println!("structured text"),
    _ => println!("not text"),
}
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [From](https://docs.rs/struct.FromStrError.html)- StrError
- An error when parsing a `Mime`from a string.
- [Mime](https://docs.rs/struct.Mime.html)
- A parsed mime or media type.
- [Mime](https://docs.rs/struct.MimeIter.html)- Iter
- An iterator of parsed mime
- [Name](https://docs.rs/struct.Name.html)
- A section of a `Mime`.
- [Params](https://docs.rs/struct.Params.html)
- An iterator over the parameters of a MIME.

[256](#256)fn eq_ascii(a: &str, b: &str) -> bool {

[263](#263)
[264](#264)    a.eq_ignore_ascii_case(b)

[266](#266)
[267](#267)fn mime_eq_str(mime: &Mime, s: &str) -> bool {
[268](#268)    if let ParamSource::Utf8(semicolon) = mime.params {
[269](#269)        if mime.source.as_ref().len() == s.len() {
[270](#270)            eq_ascii(mime.source.as_ref(), s)
[271](#271)        } else {
[272](#272)            params_eq(semicolon, mime.source.as_ref(), s)
[273](#273)        }
[274](#274)    } else if let Some(semicolon) = mime.semicolon() {
[275](#275)        params_eq(semicolon, mime.source.as_ref(), s)
[276](#276)    } else {
[277](#277)        eq_ascii(mime.source.as_ref(), s)
[278](#278)    }
[279](#279)}
[280](#280)
[281](#281)fn params_eq(semicolon: usize, a: &str, b: &str) -> bool {
[282](#282)    if b.len() < semicolon + 1 {
[283](#283)        false
[284](#284)    } else if !eq_ascii(&a[..semicolon], &b[..semicolon]) {
[285](#285)        false
[286](#286)    } else {
[287](#287)        let mut a = &a[semicolon + 1..];
[289](#289)        let mut b = &b[semicolon + 1..];
[290](#290)        let mut sensitive;
[291](#291)
[292](#292)        loop {
[293](#293)            a = a.trim();
[294](#294)            b = b.trim();
[295](#295)
[296](#296)            match (a.is_empty(), b.is_empty()) {
[297](#297)                (true, true) => return true,
[298](#298)                (true, false) |
[299](#299)                (false, true) => return false,
[300](#300)                (false, false) => (),
[301](#301)            }
[302](#302)
[303](#303)            if let Some(a_idx) = a.find('=') {
[305](#305)                let a_name = {
[306](#306)                    #[allow(deprecated)]
[307](#307)                    { a[..a_idx].trim_left() }
[308](#308)                };
[309](#309)                if let Some(b_idx) = b.find('=') {
[310](#310)                    let b_name = {
[311](#311)                        #[allow(deprecated)]
[312](#312)                        { b[..b_idx].trim_left() }
[313](#313)                    };
[314](#314)                    if !eq_ascii(a_name, b_name) {
[315](#315)                        return false;
[316](#316)                    }
[317](#317)                    sensitive = a_name != CHARSET;
[318](#318)                    a = &a[..a_idx];
[319](#319)                    b = &b[..b_idx];
[320](#320)                } else {
[321](#321)                    return false;
[322](#322)                }
[323](#323)            } else {
[324](#324)                return false;
[325](#325)            }
[326](#326)            let a_quoted = if a.as_bytes()[0] == b'"' {
[328](#328)                a = &a[1..];
[329](#329)                true
[330](#330)            } else {
[331](#331)                false
[332](#332)            };
[333](#333)            let b_quoted = if b.as_bytes()[0] == b'"' {
[334](#334)                b = &b[1..];
[335](#335)                true
[336](#336)            } else {
[337](#337)                false
[338](#338)            };
[339](#339)
[340](#340)            let a_end = if a_quoted {
[341](#341)                if let Some(quote) = a.find('"') {
[342](#342)                    quote
[343](#343)                } else {
[344](#344)                    return false;
[345](#345)                }
[346](#346)            } else {
[347](#347)                a.find(';').unwrap_or(a.len())
[348](#348)            };
[349](#349)
[350](#350)            let b_end = if b_quoted {
[351](#351)                if let Some(quote) = b.find('"') {
[352](#352)                    quote
[353](#353)                } else {
[354](#354)                    return false;
[355](#355)                }
[356](#356)            } else {
[357](#357)                b.find(';').unwrap_or(b.len())
[358](#358)            };
[359](#359)
[360](#360)            if sensitive {
[361](#361)                if !eq_ascii(&a[..a_end], &b[..b_end]) {
[362](#362)                    return false;
[363](#363)                }
[364](#364)            } else {
[365](#365)                if &a[..a_end] != &b[..b_end] {
[366](#366)                    return false;
[367](#367)                }
[368](#368)            }
[369](#369)            a = &a[a_end..];
[370](#370)            b = &b[b_end..];
[371](#371)        }
[372](#372)    }
[373](#373)}
[374](#374)

[517](#517)enum ParamsInner<'a> {
[520](#520)    Utf8,
[521](#521)    Custom {
[522](#522)        source: &'a Source,
[523](#523)        params: slice::Iter<'a, (Indexed, Indexed)>,
[524](#524)    },
[525](#525)    None,
[526](#526)}

[530](#530)
[531](#531)impl<'a> fmt::Debug for Params<'a> {

[533](#533)        fmt.debug_struct("Params").finish()
[534](#534)    }
[535](#535)}
[536](#536)
[537](#537)impl<'a> Iterator for Params<'a> {
[538](#538)    type Item = (Name<'a>, Name<'a>);
[539](#539)
[540](#540)    #[inline]
[541](#541)    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<(Name<'a>, Name<'a>)> {
[542](#542)        match self.0 {
[543](#543)            ParamsInner::Utf8 => {
[544](#544)                let value = (CHARSET, UTF_8);
[545](#545)                self.0 = ParamsInner::None;
[546](#546)                Some(value)
[547](#547)            }
[548](#548)            ParamsInner::Custom { source, ref mut params } => {
[549](#549)                params.next().map(|&(name, value)| {
[550](#550)                    let name = Name {
[551](#551)                        source: &source.as_ref()[name.0..name.1],
[552](#552)                        insensitive: true,
[553](#553)                    };
[554](#554)                    let value = Name {
[555](#555)                        source: &source.as_ref()[value.0..value.1],
[556](#556)                        insensitive: name == CHARSET,
[557](#557)                    };
[558](#558)                    (name, value)
[559](#559)                })
[560](#560)            }
[561](#561)            ParamsInner::None => None
[562](#562)        }
[563](#563)    }
[564](#564)
[565](#565)    #[inline]
[566](#566)    fn size_hint(&self) -> (usize, Option<usize>) {
[567](#567)        match self.0 {
[568](#568)            ParamsInner::Utf8 => (1, Some(1)),
[569](#569)            ParamsInner::Custom { ref params, .. } => params.size_hint(),
[570](#570)            ParamsInner::None => (0, Some(0)),
[571](#571)        }
[572](#572)    }
[573](#573)}

[686](#686)    );
[687](#687)    ($id:ident, $src:expr, $slash:expr, $plus:expr) => (

[689](#689)    );
[690](#690)
[691](#691)    ($id:ident, $src:expr, $slash:expr, $plus:expr, $params:expr) => (

[697](#697)        #[doc = "`"]
[698](#698)        #[doc = $src]
[699](#699)        #[doc = "`"]
[700](#700)        pub const $id: Mime = Mime {
[701](#701)            source: Source::Atom(__Atoms::$id as u8, $src),
[702](#702)            slash: $slash,
[703](#703)            plus: $plus,

[710](#710)#[cfg(test)]
[711](#711)macro_rules! mime_constant_test {
[712](#712)    ($id:ident, $src:expr, $slash:expr) => (
[713](#713)        mime_constant_test!($id, $src, $slash, None);
[714](#714)    );
[715](#715)    ($id:ident, $src:expr, $slash:expr, $plus:expr) => (
[716](#716)        mime_constant_test!(FULL $id, $src, $slash, $plus, ParamSource::None);
[717](#717)    );
[718](#718)
[719](#719)    ($id:ident, $src:expr, $slash:expr, $plus:expr, $params:expr) => (
[720](#720)        mime_constant_test!(FULL $id, $src, $slash, $plus, ParamSource::Utf8($params));
[721](#721)    );
[722](#722)
[723](#723)    (FULL $id:ident, $src:expr, $slash:expr, $plus:expr, $params:expr) => ({
[724](#724)        let __mime = $id;
[725](#725)        let __slash = __mime.as_ref().as_bytes()[$slash];
[726](#726)        assert_eq!(__slash, b'/', "{:?} has {:?} at slash position {:?}", __mime, __slash as char, $slash);
[727](#727)        if let Some(plus) = __mime.plus {
[728](#728)            let __c = __mime.as_ref().as_bytes()[plus];
[729](#729)            assert_eq!(__c, b'+', "{:?} has {:?} at plus position {:?}", __mime, __c as char, plus);
[730](#730)        } else {
[731](#731)            assert!(!__mime.as_ref().as_bytes().contains(&b'+'), "{:?} forgot plus", __mime);
[732](#732)        }
[733](#733)        if let ParamSource::Utf8(semicolon) = __mime.params {
[734](#734)            assert_eq!(__mime.as_ref().as_bytes()[semicolon], b';');
[735](#735)            assert_eq!(&__mime.as_ref()[semicolon..], "; charset=utf-8");
[736](#736)        } else if let ParamSource::None = __mime.params {
[737](#737)            assert!(!__mime.as_ref().as_bytes().contains(&b';'));
[738](#738)        } else {
[739](#739)            unreachable!();
[740](#740)        }
[741](#741)        __mime.atom()
[742](#742)    })

# Mime in mime - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/mime/0.3.17/mime/struct.Mime.html

`pub struct Mime { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A parsed mime or media type.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Get an optional +suffix for this `Mime`.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-2)Example

```
let svg = "image/svg+xml".parse::<mime::Mime>().unwrap();
assert_eq!(svg.suffix(), Some(mime::XML));
assert_eq!(svg.suffix().unwrap(), "xml");
assert!(mime::TEXT_PLAIN.suffix().is_none());
```
Look up a parameter by name.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-3)Example

```
let mime = mime::TEXT_PLAIN_UTF_8;
assert_eq!(mime.get_param(mime::CHARSET), Some(mime::UTF_8));
assert_eq!(mime.get_param("charset").unwrap(), "utf-8");
assert!(mime.get_param("boundary").is_none());
let mime = "multipart/form-data; boundary=ABCDEFG".parse::<mime::Mime>().unwrap();
assert_eq!(mime.get_param(mime::BOUNDARY).unwrap(), "ABCDEFG");
```
## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/mime/lib.rs.html#393-397)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-PartialOrd-for-Mime)

# Name in mime - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/mime/0.3.17/mime/struct.Name.html

`pub struct Name<'a> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A section of a `Mime`.

For instance, for the Mime `image/svg+xml`, it contains 3 `Name`s,
`image`, `svg`, and `xml`.

In most cases, `Name`s are compared ignoring case.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Get the value of this `Name` as a string.

Note that the borrow is not tied to `&self` but the `'a` lifetime, allowing the
string to outlive `Name`. Alternately, there is an `impl<'a> From<Name<'a>> for &'a str`
which isn’t rendered by Rustdoc, that can be accessed using `str::from(name)` or `name.into()`.

# mime - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/mime/latest/mime/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#mime)Mime

Mime is now Media Type, technically, but `Mime` is more immediately
understandable, so the main type here is `Mime`.

[§](https://docs.rs#what-is-mime)What is Mime?

Example mime string: `text/plain`

```
let plain_text: mime::Mime = "text/plain".parse().unwrap();
assert_eq!(plain_text, mime::TEXT_PLAIN);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#inspecting-mimes)Inspecting Mimes

```
let mime = mime::TEXT_PLAIN;
match (mime.type_(), mime.subtype()) {
    (mime::TEXT, mime::PLAIN) => println!("plain text!"),
    (mime::TEXT, _) => println!("structured text"),
    _ => println!("not text"),
}
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [From](https://docs.rs/struct.FromStrError.html)- StrError
- An error when parsing a `Mime`from a string.
- [Mime](https://docs.rs/struct.Mime.html)
- A parsed mime or media type.
- [Mime](https://docs.rs/struct.MimeIter.html)- Iter
- An iterator of parsed mime
- [Name](https://docs.rs/struct.Name.html)
- A section of a `Mime`.
- [Params](https://docs.rs/struct.Params.html)
- An iterator over the parameters of a MIME.

# mime 0.3.17 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/mime/latest/builds

All the builds on docs.rs are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The limits for this crate are the following:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                    If a build fails because it hit one of those limits please
                    [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                    to get them increased.

# mime 0.3.16 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/mime/0.3.16

# mime

Support MIME (Media Types) as strong types in Rust.

## Usage

```
extern crate mime;
// common types are constants
let text = TEXT_PLAIN;
// deconstruct Mimes to match on them
match
```
Support MIME (Media Types) as strong types in Rust.

```
extern crate mime;
// common types are constants
let text = mime::TEXT_PLAIN;
// deconstruct Mimes to match on them
match (text.type_(), text.subtype()) {
    (mime::TEXT, mime::PLAIN) => {
        // plain text!
    },
    (mime::TEXT, _) => {
        // structured text!
    },
    _ => {
        // not text!
    }
}
```

# mime 0.3.5 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/mime/0.3.5

# mime

Support MIME (Media Types) as strong types in Rust.

## Usage

```
extern crate mime;
// common types are constants
let text = TEXT_PLAIN;
// deconstruct Mimes to match on them
match
```
Support MIME (Media Types) as strong types in Rust.

```
extern crate mime;
// common types are constants
let text = mime::TEXT_PLAIN;
// deconstruct Mimes to match on them
match (text.type_(), text.subtype()) {
    (mime::TEXT, mime::PLAIN) => {
        // plain text!
    },
    (mime::TEXT, _) => {
        // structured text!
    },
    _ => {
        // not text!
    }
}
```

# mime - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/mime

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#mime)Mime

Mime is now Media Type, technically, but `Mime` is more immediately
understandable, so the main type here is `Mime`.

[§](https://docs.rs#what-is-mime)What is Mime?

Example mime string: `text/plain`

```
let plain_text: mime::Mime = "text/plain".parse().unwrap();
assert_eq!(plain_text, mime::TEXT_PLAIN);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#inspecting-mimes)Inspecting Mimes

```
let mime = mime::TEXT_PLAIN;
match (mime.type_(), mime.subtype()) {
    (mime::TEXT, mime::PLAIN) => println!("plain text!"),
    (mime::TEXT, _) => println!("structured text"),
    _ => println!("not text"),
}
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [From](https://docs.rs/struct.FromStrError.html)- StrError
- An error when parsing a `Mime`from a string.
- [Mime](https://docs.rs/struct.Mime.html)
- A parsed mime or media type.
- [Mime](https://docs.rs/struct.MimeIter.html)- Iter
- An iterator of parsed mime
- [Name](https://docs.rs/struct.Name.html)
- A section of a `Mime`.
- [Params](https://docs.rs/struct.Params.html)
- An iterator over the parameters of a MIME.

# mime 0.3.17 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/mime/latest/source/README.md

```
[![Build Status](https://travis-ci.org/hyperium/mime.svg?branch=master)](https://travis-ci.org/hyperium/mime)
[![crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/mime.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/mime)
[![docs.rs](https://docs.rs/mime/badge.svg)](https://docs.rs/mime)
Support MIME (Media Types) as strong types in Rust.
[Documentation](https://docs.rs/mime)
```rust
extern crate mime;
// common types are constants
let text = mime::TEXT_PLAIN;
// deconstruct Mimes to match on them
match (text.type_(), text.subtype()) {
}
```
```

---

# mime - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/mime/latest/target-redirect/mime/index.html

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#mime)Mime

Mime is now Media Type, technically, but `Mime` is more immediately
understandable, so the main type here is `Mime`.

[§](https://docs.rs#what-is-mime)What is Mime?

Example mime string: `text/plain`

```
let plain_text: mime::Mime = "text/plain".parse().unwrap();
assert_eq!(plain_text, mime::TEXT_PLAIN);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#inspecting-mimes)Inspecting Mimes

```
let mime = mime::TEXT_PLAIN;
match (mime.type_(), mime.subtype()) {
    (mime::TEXT, mime::PLAIN) => println!("plain text!"),
    (mime::TEXT, _) => println!("structured text"),
    _ => println!("not text"),
}
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [From](https://docs.rs/struct.FromStrError.html)- StrError
- An error when parsing a `Mime`from a string.
- [Mime](https://docs.rs/struct.Mime.html)
- A parsed mime or media type.
- [Mime](https://docs.rs/struct.MimeIter.html)- Iter
- An iterator of parsed mime
- [Name](https://docs.rs/struct.Name.html)
- A section of a `Mime`.
- [Params](https://docs.rs/struct.Params.html)
- An iterator over the parameters of a MIME.

[112](#112)            Source::Atom(_, s) => s,
[113](#113)            Source::Dynamic(ref s) => s,
[114](#114)        }
[115](#115)    }
[116](#116)}
[117](#117)
[118](#118)#[derive(Clone)]
[119](#119)enum ParamSource {
[120](#120)    Utf8(usize),
[121](#121)    Custom(usize, Vec<(Indexed, Indexed)>),
[122](#122)    None,
[123](#123)}
[124](#124)
[125](#125)#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
[126](#126)struct Indexed(usize, usize);
[127](#127)
[128](#128)impl Mime {
[129](#129)    #[inline]
[139](#139)    pub fn type_(&self) -> Name {
[140](#140)        Name {
[141](#141)            source: &self.source.as_ref()[..self.slash],
[142](#142)            insensitive: true,
[143](#143)        }
[144](#144)    }
[145](#145)
[146](#146)    #[inline]
[156](#156)    pub fn subtype(&self) -> Name {
[157](#157)        let end = self.plus.unwrap_or_else(|| {
[158](#158)            return self.semicolon().unwrap_or(self.source.as_ref().len())
[159](#159)        });
[160](#160)        Name {
[161](#161)            source: &self.source.as_ref()[self.slash + 1..end],
[162](#162)            insensitive: true,
[163](#163)        }
[164](#164)    }
[165](#165)
[166](#166)    #[inline]
[179](#179)    pub fn suffix(&self) -> Option<Name> {
[180](#180)        let end = self.semicolon().unwrap_or(self.source.as_ref().len());
[181](#181)        self.plus.map(|idx| Name {
[182](#182)            source: &self.source.as_ref()[idx + 1..end],
[183](#183)            insensitive: true,
[184](#184)        })
[185](#185)    }
[186](#186)
[187](#187)    pub fn get_param<'a, N>(&'a self, attr: N) -> Option<Name<'a>>
[201](#201)    where N: PartialEq<Name<'a>> {
[202](#202)        self.params().find(|e| attr == e.0).map(|e| e.1)
[203](#203)    }
[204](#204)
[205](#205)    #[inline]
[207](#207)    pub fn params<'a>(&'a self) -> Params<'a> {
[208](#208)        let inner = match self.params {
[209](#209)            ParamSource::Utf8(_) => ParamsInner::Utf8,
[210](#210)            ParamSource::Custom(_, ref params) => {
[211](#211)                ParamsInner::Custom {
[212](#212)                    source: &self.source,
[213](#213)                    params: params.iter(),
[214](#214)                }
[215](#215)            }
[216](#216)            ParamSource::None => ParamsInner::None,
[217](#217)        };
[218](#218)
[219](#219)        Params(inner)
[220](#220)    }
[221](#221)
[222](#222)    pub fn essence_str(&self) -> &str {
[226](#226)        let end = self.semicolon().unwrap_or(self.source.as_ref().len());
[227](#227)
[228](#228)        &self.source.as_ref()[..end]
[229](#229)    }
[230](#230)
[231](#231)    #[cfg(test)]
[232](#232)    fn has_params(&self) -> bool {
[233](#233)        match self.params {
[234](#234)            ParamSource::None => false,
[235](#235)            _ => true,
[236](#236)        }
[237](#237)    }
[238](#238)
[239](#239)    #[inline]
[240](#240)    fn semicolon(&self) -> Option<usize> {
[241](#241)        match self.params {
[242](#242)            ParamSource::Utf8(i) |
[243](#243)            ParamSource::Custom(i, _) => Some(i),
[244](#244)            ParamSource::None => None,
[245](#245)        }
[246](#246)    }
[247](#247)
[248](#248)    fn atom(&self) -> u8 {
[249](#249)        match self.source {
[250](#250)            Source::Atom(a, _) => a,
[251](#251)            _ => 0,
[252](#252)        }
[253](#253)    }
[254](#254)}
[255](#255)
[256](#256)fn eq_ascii(a: &str, b: &str) -> bool {
[259](#259)    #[allow(deprecated, unused)]
[262](#262)    use std::ascii::AsciiExt;
[263](#263)
[264](#264)    a.eq_ignore_ascii_case(b)
[265](#265)}
[266](#266)
[267](#267)fn mime_eq_str(mime: &Mime, s: &str) -> bool {
[268](#268)    if let ParamSource::Utf8(semicolon) = mime.params {
[269](#269)        if mime.source.as_ref().len() == s.len() {
[270](#270)            eq_ascii(mime.source.as_ref(), s)
[271](#271)        } else {
[272](#272)            params_eq(semicolon, mime.source.as_ref(), s)
[273](#273)        }
[274](#274)    } else if let Some(semicolon) = mime.semicolon() {
[275](#275)        params_eq(semicolon, mime.source.as_ref(), s)
[276](#276)    } else {
[277](#277)        eq_ascii(mime.source.as_ref(), s)
[278](#278)    }
[279](#279)}
[280](#280)
[281](#281)fn params_eq(semicolon: usize, a: &str, b: &str) -> bool {
[282](#282)    if b.len() < semicolon + 1 {
[283](#283)        false
[284](#284)    } else if !eq_ascii(&a[..semicolon], &b[..semicolon]) {
[285](#285)        false
[286](#286)    } else {
[287](#287)        let mut a = &a[semicolon + 1..];
[289](#289)        let mut b = &b[semicolon + 1..];
[290](#290)        let mut sensitive;
[291](#291)
[292](#292)        loop {
[293](#293)            a = a.trim();
[294](#294)            b = b.trim();
[295](#295)
[296](#296)            match (a.is_empty(), b.is_empty()) {
[297](#297)                (true, true) => return true,
[298](#298)                (true, false) |
[299](#299)                (false, true) => return false,
[300](#300)                (false, false) => (),
[301](#301)            }
[302](#302)
[303](#303)            if let Some(a_idx) = a.find('=') {
[305](#305)                let a_name = {
[306](#306)                    #[allow(deprecated)]
[307](#307)                    { a[..a_idx].trim_left() }
[308](#308)                };
[309](#309)                if let Some(b_idx) = b.find('=') {
[310](#310)                    let b_name = {
[311](#311)                        #[allow(deprecated)]
[312](#312)                        { b[..b_idx].trim_left() }
[313](#313)                    };
[314](#314)                    if !eq_ascii(a_name, b_name) {
[315](#315)                        return false;
[316](#316)                    }
[317](#317)                    sensitive = a_name != CHARSET;
[318](#318)                    a = &a[..a_idx];
[319](#319)                    b = &b[..b_idx];
[320](#320)                } else {
[321](#321)                    return false;
[322](#322)                }
[323](#323)            } else {
[324](#324)                return false;
[325](#325)            }
[326](#326)            let a_quoted = if a.as_bytes()[0] == b'"' {
[328](#328)                a = &a[1..];
[329](#329)                true
[330](#330)            } else {
[331](#331)                false
[332](#332)            };
[333](#333)            let b_quoted = if b.as_bytes()[0] == b'"' {
[334](#334)                b = &b[1..];
[335](#335)                true
[336](#336)            } else {
[337](#337)                false
[338](#338)            };
[339](#339)
[340](#340)            let a_end = if a_quoted {
[341](#341)                if let Some(quote) = a.find('"') {
[342](#342)                    quote
[343](#343)                } else {
[344](#344)                    return false;
[345](#345)                }
[346](#346)            } else {
[347](#347)                a.find(';').unwrap_or(a.len())
[348](#348)            };
[349](#349)
[350](#350)            let b_end = if b_quoted {
[351](#351)                if let Some(quote) = b.find('"') {
[352](#352)                    quote
[353](#353)                } else {
[354](#354)                    return false;
[355](#355)                }
[356](#356)            } else {
[357](#357)                b.find(';').unwrap_or(b.len())
[358](#358)            };
[359](#359)
[360](#360)            if sensitive {
[361](#361)                if !eq_ascii(&a[..a_end], &b[..b_end]) {
[362](#362)                    return false;
[363](#363)                }
[364](#364)            } else {
[365](#365)                if &a[..a_end] != &b[..b_end] {
[366](#366)                    return false;
[367](#367)                }
[368](#368)            }
[369](#369)            a = &a[a_end..];
[370](#370)            b = &b[b_end..];
[371](#371)        }
[372](#372)    }
[373](#373)}
[374](#374)
[375](#375)impl PartialEq for Mime {
[376](#376)    #[inline]
[377](#377)    fn eq(&self, other: &Mime) -> bool {
[378](#378)        match (self.atom(), other.atom()) {
[379](#379)            (0, _) |
[385](#385)            (_, 0) => mime_eq_str(self, other.source.as_ref()),
[386](#386)            (a, b) => a == b,
[387](#387)        }
[388](#388)    }

[516](#516)
[517](#517)enum ParamsInner<'a> {
[520](#520)    Utf8,
[521](#521)    Custom {
[522](#522)        source: &'a Source,
[523](#523)        params: slice::Iter<'a, (Indexed, Indexed)>,
[524](#524)    },
[525](#525)    None,
[526](#526)}
[527](#527)
[528](#528)pub struct Params<'a>(ParamsInner<'a>);
[530](#530)
[531](#531)impl<'a> fmt::Debug for Params<'a> {
[532](#532)    fn fmt(&self, fmt: &mut fmt::Formatter) -> fmt::Result {
[533](#533)        fmt.debug_struct("Params").finish()
[534](#534)    }
[535](#535)}
[536](#536)
[537](#537)impl<'a> Iterator for Params<'a> {
[538](#538)    type Item = (Name<'a>, Name<'a>);
[539](#539)
[540](#540)    #[inline]
[541](#541)    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<(Name<'a>, Name<'a>)> {
[542](#542)        match self.0 {
[543](#543)            ParamsInner::Utf8 => {
[544](#544)                let value = (CHARSET, UTF_8);
[545](#545)                self.0 = ParamsInner::None;
[546](#546)                Some(value)
[547](#547)            }
[548](#548)            ParamsInner::Custom { source, ref mut params } => {
[549](#549)                params.next().map(|&(name, value)| {
[550](#550)                    let name = Name {
[551](#551)                        source: &source.as_ref()[name.0..name.1],
[552](#552)                        insensitive: true,
[553](#553)                    };
[554](#554)                    let value = Name {
[555](#555)                        source: &source.as_ref()[value.0..value.1],
[556](#556)                        insensitive: name == CHARSET,
[557](#557)                    };
[558](#558)                    (name, value)
[559](#559)                })
[560](#560)            }
[561](#561)            ParamsInner::None => None
[562](#562)        }
[563](#563)    }
[564](#564)
[565](#565)    #[inline]
[566](#566)    fn size_hint(&self) -> (usize, Option<usize>) {
[567](#567)        match self.0 {
[568](#568)            ParamsInner::Utf8 => (1, Some(1)),
[569](#569)            ParamsInner::Custom { ref params, .. } => params.size_hint(),
[570](#570)            ParamsInner::None => (0, Some(0)),
[571](#571)        }
[572](#572)    }
[573](#573)}

[653](#653)    ($($id:ident, $($piece:expr),*;)*) => (
[654](#654)        #[allow(non_camel_case_types)]
[655](#655)        enum __Atoms {
[656](#656)            __Dynamic,
[657](#657)        $(
[658](#658)            $id,
[659](#659)        )*
[660](#660)        }
[661](#661)
[662](#662)        $(
[663](#663)            mime_constant! {
[664](#664)                $id, $($piece),*
[665](#665)            }
[666](#666)        )*
[667](#667)
[668](#668)        #[test]
[669](#669)        fn test_mimes_macro_consts() {
[670](#670)            let _ = [
[671](#671)            $(
[672](#672)            mime_constant_test! {
[673](#673)                $id, $($piece),*
[674](#674)            }
[675](#675)            ),*
[676](#676)            ].iter().enumerate().map(|(pos, &atom)| {
[677](#677)                assert_eq!(pos + 1, atom as usize, "atom {} in position {}", atom, pos + 1);
[678](#678)            }).collect::<Vec<()>>();
[679](#679)        }
[680](#680)    )

[683](#683)macro_rules! mime_constant {
[684](#684)    ($id:ident, $src:expr, $slash:expr) => (
[685](#685)        mime_constant!($id, $src, $slash, None);
[686](#686)    );
[687](#687)    ($id:ident, $src:expr, $slash:expr, $plus:expr) => (
[688](#688)        mime_constant!(FULL $id, $src, $slash, $plus, ParamSource::None);
[689](#689)    );
[690](#690)
[691](#691)    ($id:ident, $src:expr, $slash:expr, $plus:expr, $params:expr) => (
[692](#692)        mime_constant!(FULL $id, $src, $slash, $plus, ParamSource::Utf8($params));
[693](#693)    );
[694](#694)
[695](#695)
[696](#696)    (FULL $id:ident, $src:expr, $slash:expr, $plus:expr, $params:expr) => (
[697](#697)        #[doc = "`"]
[698](#698)        #[doc = $src]
[699](#699)        #[doc = "`"]
[700](#700)        pub const $id: Mime = Mime {
[701](#701)            source: Source::Atom(__Atoms::$id as u8, $src),
[702](#702)            slash: $slash,
[703](#703)            plus: $plus,
[704](#704)            params: $params,
[705](#705)        };
[706](#706)    )
[707](#707)}
[708](#708)
[709](#709)
[710](#710)#[cfg(test)]
[711](#711)macro_rules! mime_constant_test {
[712](#712)    ($id:ident, $src:expr, $slash:expr) => (
[713](#713)        mime_constant_test!($id, $src, $slash, None);
[714](#714)    );
[715](#715)    ($id:ident, $src:expr, $slash:expr, $plus:expr) => (
[716](#716)        mime_constant_test!(FULL $id, $src, $slash, $plus, ParamSource::None);
[717](#717)    );
[718](#718)
[719](#719)    ($id:ident, $src:expr, $slash:expr, $plus:expr, $params:expr) => (
[720](#720)        mime_constant_test!(FULL $id, $src, $slash, $plus, ParamSource::Utf8($params));
[721](#721)    );
[722](#722)
[723](#723)    (FULL $id:ident, $src:expr, $slash:expr, $plus:expr, $params:expr) => ({
[724](#724)        let __mime = $id;
[725](#725)        let __slash = __mime.as_ref().as_bytes()[$slash];
[726](#726)        assert_eq!(__slash, b'/', "{:?} has {:?} at slash position {:?}", __mime, __slash as char, $slash);
[727](#727)        if let Some(plus) = __mime.plus {
[728](#728)            let __c = __mime.as_ref().as_bytes()[plus];
[729](#729)            assert_eq!(__c, b'+', "{:?} has {:?} at plus position {:?}", __mime, __c as char, plus);
[730](#730)        } else {
[731](#731)            assert!(!__mime.as_ref().as_bytes().contains(&b'+'), "{:?} forgot plus", __mime);
[732](#732)        }
[733](#733)        if let ParamSource::Utf8(semicolon) = __mime.params {
[734](#734)            assert_eq!(__mime.as_ref().as_bytes()[semicolon], b';');
[735](#735)            assert_eq!(&__mime.as_ref()[semicolon..], "; charset=utf-8");
[736](#736)        } else if let ParamSource::None = __mime.params {
[737](#737)            assert!(!__mime.as_ref().as_bytes().contains(&b';'));
[738](#738)        } else {
[739](#739)            unreachable!();
[740](#740)        }
[741](#741)        __mime.atom()
[742](#742)    })
[743](#743)}

# Name in mime - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/mime/latest/target-redirect/mime/struct.Name.html

`pub struct Name<'a> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A section of a `Mime`.

For instance, for the Mime `image/svg+xml`, it contains 3 `Name`s,
`image`, `svg`, and `xml`.

In most cases, `Name`s are compared ignoring case.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Get the value of this `Name` as a string.

Note that the borrow is not tied to `&self` but the `'a` lifetime, allowing the
string to outlive `Name`. Alternately, there is an `impl<'a> From<Name<'a>> for &'a str`
which isn’t rendered by Rustdoc, that can be accessed using `str::from(name)` or `name.into()`.

## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

`iter_order_by`)[Lexicographically](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cmp/trait.Ord.html#lexicographical-comparison)compares the

[elements of this](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cmp/trait.PartialOrd.html)

`PartialOrd`[with those of another. The comparison works like short-circuit evaluation, returning a result without comparing the remaining elements. As soon as an order can be determined, the evaluation stops and a result is returned.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/iterator/trait.Iterator.html)

# clap - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/clap

## Expand description

Command Line Argument Parser for Rust

Quick Links:

- Derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)
- Builder [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/struct.Command.html)
- [Cookbook](https://docs.rs/_cookbook/index.html)
- [CLI Concepts](https://docs.rs/_concepts/index.html)
- [FAQ](https://docs.rs/_faq/index.html)
- [Discussions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/discussions)
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/blob/v4.6.1/CHANGELOG.md)(includes major version migration guides)

[§](https://docs.rs#aspirations)Aspirations

- Out of the box, users get a polished CLI experience
- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output, [shell completions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/tree/master/clap_complete), etc

- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output,
- Flexible enough to port your existing CLI interface
- However, we won’t necessarily streamline support for each use case

- Reasonable parse performance
- Resilient maintainership, including
- Willing to break compatibility rather than batching up breaking changes in large releases
- Leverage feature flags to keep to one active branch
- Being under [WG-CLI](https://github.com/rust-cli/team/)to increase the bus factor

- We follow semver and will wait about 6-9 months between major breaking changes
- We will support the last two minor Rust releases (MSRV, currently 1.74)

While these aspirations can be at odds with fast build times and low binary
size, we will still strive to keep these reasonable for the flexibility you
get.  Check out the
[argparse-benchmarks](https://github.com/rust-cli/argparse-benchmarks-rs) for
CLI parsers optimized for other use cases.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Run

`$ cargo add clap --features derive`*(See also  feature flag reference)*

Then define your CLI in `main.rs`:

```
use clap::Parser;
/// Simple program to greet a person
#[derive(Parser, Debug)]
#[command(version, about, long_about = None)]
struct Args {
    /// Name of the person to greet
    #[arg(short, long)]
    name: String,
    /// Number of times to greet
    #[arg(short, long, default_value_t = 1)]
    count: u8,
}
fn main() {
    let args = Args::parse();
    for _ in 0..args.count {
        println!("Hello {}!", args.name);
    }
}
```
And try it out:

```
$ demo --help
A simple to use, efficient, and full-featured Command Line Argument Parser
Usage: demo[EXE] [OPTIONS] --name <NAME>
Options:
  -n, --name <NAME>    Name of the person to greet
  -c, --count <COUNT>  Number of times to greet [default: 1]
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
$ demo --name Me
Hello Me!
```
*(version number and  .exe extension on windows replaced by placeholders)*

See also the derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html) and [reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)

[§](https://docs.rs#related-projects)Related Projects

Augment clap:

- [wild](https://crates.io/crates/wild)for supporting wildcards (- `*`) on Windows like you do Linux
- [argfile](https://crates.io/crates/argfile)for loading additional arguments from a file (aka response files)
- [shadow-rs](https://crates.io/crates/shadow-rs)for generating- `Command::long_version`
- [clap_mangen](https://crates.io/crates/clap_mangen)for generating man page source (roff)
- [clap_complete](https://crates.io/crates/clap_complete)for shell completion support
- [clap-i18n-richformatter](https://crates.io/crates/clap-i18n-richformatter)for i18n support with- `clap::error::RichFormatter`

CLI Helpers

- [clio](https://crates.io/crates/clio)for reading/writing to files specified as arguments
- [clap-verbosity-flag](https://crates.io/crates/clap-verbosity-flag)
- [clap-cargo](https://crates.io/crates/clap-cargo)
- [colorchoice-clap](https://crates.io/crates/colorchoice-clap)

Testing

- `trycmd`
- `snapbox`
- `assert_cmd`- `assert_fs`

Documentation:

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [_concepts](https://docs.rs/_concepts/index.html)- `unstable-doc`
- CLI Concepts
- [_cookbook](https://docs.rs/_cookbook/index.html)- `unstable-doc`
- Documentation: Cookbook

- Documentation: FAQ
- [_features](https://docs.rs/_features/index.html)- `unstable-doc`
- Documentation: Feature Flags

- Tutorial for the Builder API
- [builder](https://docs.rs/builder/index.html)
- Define `Command`[arguments](https://docs.rs/struct.Arg.html)
- [error](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)
- Error reporting

- `Command`

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [arg](https://docs.rs/macro.arg.html)
- Create an `Arg`
- [command](https://docs.rs/macro.command.html)- `cargo`
- Allows you to build the `Command`instance from your Cargo.toml at compile time.
- [crate_](https://docs.rs/macro.crate_authors.html)- authors - `cargo`
- Allows you to pull the authors for the command from your Cargo.toml at
compile time in the form:
`"author1 lastname <author1@example.com>:author2 lastname <author2@example.com>"`
- [crate_](https://docs.rs/macro.crate_description.html)- description - `cargo`
- Allows you to pull the description from your Cargo.toml at compile time.
- [crate_](https://docs.rs/macro.crate_name.html)- name - `cargo`
- Allows you to pull the name from your Cargo.toml at compile time.
- [crate_](https://docs.rs/macro.crate_version.html)- version - `cargo`
- Allows you to pull the version from your Cargo.toml at compile time as
`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH_PKGVERSION_PRE`
- [value_](https://docs.rs/macro.value_parser.html)- parser
- Select a `ValueParser`

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Arg](https://docs.rs/struct.Arg.html)
- The abstract representation of a command line argument. Used to set all the options and relationships that define a valid argument for the program.
- [ArgGroup](https://docs.rs/struct.ArgGroup.html)
- Specifies a logical group of [arguments](https://docs.rs/struct.Arg.html)
- [ArgMatches](https://docs.rs/struct.ArgMatches.html)
- Container for parse results.
- [Command](https://docs.rs/struct.Command.html)
- Build a command-line interface.
- [Id](https://docs.rs/struct.Id.html)
- `Arg`- `ArgGroup`

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [ArgAction](https://docs.rs/enum.ArgAction.html)
- Behavior of arguments when they are encountered while parsing
- [Color](https://docs.rs/enum.ColorChoice.html)- Choice
- Represents the color preferences for program output
- [Value](https://docs.rs/enum.ValueHint.html)- Hint
- Provide shell with hint on how to complete an argument.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Args](https://docs.rs/trait.Args.html)
- Parse a set of arguments into a user-defined container.
- [Command](https://docs.rs/trait.CommandFactory.html)- Factory
- Create a `Command`
- [From](https://docs.rs/trait.FromArgMatches.html)- ArgMatches
- Converts an instance of `ArgMatches`
- [Parser](https://docs.rs/trait.Parser.html)
- Parse command-line arguments into `Self`.
- [Subcommand](https://docs.rs/trait.Subcommand.html)
- Parse a sub-command into a user-defined enum.
- [Value](https://docs.rs/trait.ValueEnum.html)- Enum
- Parse arguments into enums.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Error](https://docs.rs/type.Error.html)
- Command Line Argument Parser Error

/// Simple program to greet a person
#[derive(Parser, Debug)]
#[command(version, about, long_about = None)]
struct Args {
    /// Name of the person to greet
    #[arg(short, long)]
    name: String,
    /// Number of times to greet
    #[arg(short, long, default_value_t = 1)]
    count: u8,
}
fn main() {
    let args = Args::parse();
    for _ in 0..args.count {
        println!("Hello {}!", args.name);
    }
}
```
And try it out:

```
$ demo --help
A simple to use, efficient, and full-featured Command Line Argument Parser
Usage: demo[EXE] [OPTIONS] --name <NAME>
Options:
  -n, --name <NAME>    Name of the person to greet
  -c, --count <COUNT>  Number of times to greet [default: 1]
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
$ demo --name Me
Hello Me!
```
*(version number and  .exe extension on windows replaced by placeholders)*

See also the derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html) and [reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)
